title: Kushan Empire
capsule: The Kushan Empire was established by the Yuezhi chief Kujula Kadphises (fl. c. 30–80 CE) who unified the five Yuezhi tribes in Bactria and conquered Gandhara and the Kabul Valley, creating a state that at its height under Kanishka I (fl. c. 127–150 CE) extended from Sogdia through Afghanistan into the Gangetic plain as far as Varanasi. Kanishka convened a major Buddhist council, promoted Gandharan art — fusing Hellenistic, Iranian, and Indian idioms — and maintained commercial links on both the Silk Roads and Indian Ocean networks. Kushan power fragmented after c. 225 CE as the Sasanian Empire overran the western provinces and established the Kushano-Sasanian kingdom; the eastern Kushans maintained rule in the Punjab until displaced by the Kidarites in the mid-fourth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territorial extent in Bactria, Gandhara, and the northern Punjab is well attested by coinage, inscriptions (notably the Rabatak inscription), and Kushan-period archaeological sites; the eastern limit in the Gangetic plain and the precise northern boundary in Sogdia are reconstructed from coin distribution and remain approximate.
